_unit: Year-round — Tier A course skill language
_activity: Vocab Match — The Six Graded Skills
_licence: ORIGINAL. Exact wording copied from US11R_Glossary_v2_2026-09-02, Tier A, so it reads the same everywhere it appears. No new content.
intro: Match each skill line to what it actually asks you to do.

right.label: Warm up the document — set the scene before you argue
Take a clear position and hold it
Name it. Pull a specific detail. Use it as evidence
The "so what." Say why each piece of evidence matters
Bring in something from your own knowledge, not in the documents
Name it out loud — don't imply it

rationale.a: Historical Context sets the scene — the circumstances around the document — before you make an argument.
rationale.b: Thesis is a clear, held position, not just a topic.
rationale.c: Document Use means naming a specific detail from a document and using it as evidence, not just gesturing at the source.
rationale.d: Explanation is the "so what" — why the evidence matters, not just that it exists.
rationale.e: Outside Evidence is knowledge from beyond the documents themselves — what the exam calls "outside information."
rationale.f: Civic Principle has to be named out loud ("federalism," "equal protection") — implying it isn't enough.
